text:
**Findings**

High: [jobwatch/reports.py](/work/jobwatch/reports.py:14), [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:118) - timestamps are stored and compared as ISO strings, so offset-aware timestamps compare lexicographically instead of by actual instant; reports/windows can exclude or order jobs incorrectly.

Medium: [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:66) - out-of-order same-rank updates can regress a newer `RUNNING` snapshot to older elapsed/resource values.

Medium: [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:148), [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:110) - negative `AllocCPUS` and `gres/gpu=-N` are accepted, producing negative CPU/GPU-hour reports.

Medium: [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:40) - unknown states default to terminal rank, so typos/new Slurm states can incorrectly override or block lifecycle updates.

Low: [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:152) - empty `User` and `Partition` fields are accepted and persisted, creating misleading report buckets.

Low: [jobwatch/cli.py](/work/jobwatch/cli.py:121) - report commands call `db.connect`, which creates a new empty database for a mistyped path instead of failing clearly.

Low: [jobwatch/__init__.py](/work/jobwatch/__init__.py:3), [pyproject.toml](/work/pyproject.toml:7) - package version is duplicated and can drift.

**Quality Score:** 7/10

The project is small, readable, and has a useful test suite: `61 passed`. SQL injection risk looks low because dynamic SQL is whitelisted and values are parameterized. I would not approve as-is because the timestamp comparison and ingestion regression issues can produce incorrect operational reports.

Estimated rewrite/significant-change size: about 120 lines, mostly parser validation, timestamp normalization/storage, upsert ordering semantics, and tests.
